# Networking

## Core ideas and reasoning

A network connects devices to exchange data and share resources under communication rules called protocols. A LAN serves a limited local area; a WAN connects across wider geographic areas. A network interface connects a device to a network. A switch forwards Ethernet frames using learned MAC addresses; a router forwards packets between IP networks. A modem adapts signals for a particular communication medium. Distinguish these functions even when one home device combines them. Wired links may offer predictable performance; wireless links support mobility but depend on coverage, interference and security. Bandwidth describes a link's capacity, while actual throughput may be lower due to overhead, contention and loss. A client requests a service and a server provides it. A star topology connects nodes to a central device, so one branch failure usually affects only that node, while central-device failure affects the network segment. Network benefits include sharing files and printers, but require access control, maintenance and backups. Explain advantages in relation to users and data, not simply that networking is fast.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

Distinguish a LAN from a WAN.

A LAN connects devices over a limited area such as a school building. A WAN connects networks across larger geographic areas, such as branches in different towns.

### Example 2

Distinguish a switch from a router.

A switch forwards frames within a LAN using MAC addresses. A router forwards packets between networks using IP routing information.

### Example 3

State one benefit and one risk of a star network.

A failed branch cable typically isolates only one device. Failure of the central switch can disrupt communication for all devices attached to it.

### Example 4

Explain the function of a network interface card.

It provides the interface that connects a computer to a network so it can send and receive data.

## Check your reasoning

Explain why the method applies before calculating or naming a result. Compare with a contrasting case. For calculations carry units, keep intermediate precision, then check by substitution, conservation or a second route. Describe observations separately from their explanation.
